newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: TML, Pearson talks said advanced.
newsitem.headline: TML, Pearson talks said advanced.

text.p: Pearson Plc, publisher of the Financial Times, and Times Media Ltd (TML) plan to parcel off TML's business publications into a new jointly-controlled company, a former TML board member said on Thursday.

Nigel Bruce, who resigned form the TML board on Wednesday and as editor of the weekly Financial Mail, said Pearson and TML would both have a 50 percent stake in the company controlling Business Day newspaper and Financial Mail.

"If the deal comes through, the financial publications of TML will be (jointly) owned by Pearsons," he told a news conference to announce his acceptance of the editorship of rival Finance Week, bought recently by ex-colleague David Gleason.
Bruce, who resigned from the Financial Mail on Wednesday following disagreements with management, said he did not know how long it would be before the deal between TML and Pearson was concluded.

The National Empowerment Consortium (NEC), a grouping of black business interests, last month won control of Johnnies Industrial Corporation -- which in turn controls TML -- by buying a 35 percent stake.
Bruce said new Johnnic chairman Cyril Ramaphosa had given a personal undertaking to Pearson to protect editorial independence.
TML executives were not immediately available to comment.
